papers.title: Perinatal suicide risk factors: A network analysis
papers.abstract: Purpose Suicide during pregnancy or after birth (the perinatal period) represents a leading, preventable cause of United States maternal deaths. This study aimed to understand the complex relationship between perinatal status and life circumstances among perinatal suicide decedents in the United States and generate insights regarding suicide risk. Methods This cross-sectional study used decedent data from the 2003-2023 National Violent Death Reporting System suicide mortality registry (N=20,217). We applied psychometric network analysis using 18 binary life circumstances indicators representing four domains: relationships, health, socioeconomic status, and risk factors for suicide. We generated two networks for the overall sample and perinatal sample and assessed network structure, bridge centralities, and stability. Results The analytic sample included 1,297 perinatal and 18,920 non-perinatal decedents. The network of the overall sample was stable. Perinatal status did not appear at the center of the network but connected primarily with intimate partner problems. The network of the perinatal sample was modestly stable. Postpartum status was not at the center of the network but connected to depressed mood and mental health diagnoses. In both networks, depressed mood had the highest bridge betweenness, and there was a consistent link between physical health domains and socioeconomic domains. Conclusion Suicide prevention strategies targeting childbearing-aged women should incorporate factors beyond pregnancy, including physical health, intimate partner relationships, and socioeconomic challenges.

papers.title: Validation of gender identity and sexual behavior stigma measures among transgender women in the United States: Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses
papers.abstract: Introduction Transgender women experience stigma related to both gender identity and sexual behavior, yet robust measurement tools remain limited. This study evaluated the factor structure and external construct validity of the Measures of Attributional Stigma for gender identity (MAS-GI) and sexual behavior (MAS-SB) among transgender women in the United States. Methods We analyzed cross-sectional data from the Transgender Womens Internet Survey and Testing (TWIST) platform collected from 2023-2025 (N=2,901). Participants completed parallel 14-item stigma measures attributed separately to gender identity and sexual behavior. The sample was split into exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n=1,951; 2023-2024) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n=950; 2024-2025) samples. External construct validity was evaluated via associations with depression symptoms, posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), social capital, transgender identity pride, and healthcare utilization. Results EFA identified three MAS-GI factors (family stigma, anticipated healthcare stigma, and enacted social stigma) and two MAS-SB factors (global healthcare stigma and social/institutional stigma). CFA confirmed both structures with good to excellent model fit. All stigma dimensions were positively associated with depression and PTSD. Anticipated healthcare and enacted social stigma from the MAS-GI and both MAS-SB dimensions were negatively associated with social capital. Greater anticipated gender identity healthcare stigma associated with lower transgender identity pride. Several stigma dimensions were also positively associated with HIV/STI testing, PrEP use, and mental healthcare utilization. Conclusions The MAS-GI and MAS-SB demonstrate factorial validity and preliminary external construct validity among transgender women. These measures enable precise assessment of stigma by attribution and source and inform stigma surveillance and intervention evaluation.

papers.title: Moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, longitudinal blood pressure trajectories, and hypertension-related outcomes in older adults at high cardiovascular risk: a cohort study
papers.abstract: Background: We aimed to investigate the association between moderate-to-vigorous leisure-time physical activity (MVLTPA) and longitudinal trajectories of systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) blood pressure, as well as the incidence of high blood pressure and antihypertensive drug initiation, in adults aged 60-80 years at high cardiovascular risk. Methods: In participants from the PREDIMED trial (61% women; 5,254 participants), MVLTPA was assessed using the Minnesota Leisure Time Physical Activity Questionnaire and expressed as cumulative average metabolic equivalent of task-minutes/day. SBP and DBP trajectories were modelled using mixed-effects models with cubic splines (>100 [adequate] vs 140 mmHg or DBP >90 mmHg) and antihypertensive drug initiation were assessed with Cox models (adequate vs insufficient, and continuous MVLTPA). Results: SBP and DBP declined with increasing age, with no clinically meaningful differences between MVLTPA groups. The association between adequate MVLTPA and incident high blood pressure was null (HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.94-1.32). However, adequate MVLTPA was associated with a 17% lower risk of antihypertensive drug initiation (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71-0.98). The association appeared stronger in women (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58-0.94) than in men (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.78-1.22) (p-value for sex interaction = 0.058). A modest inverse linear dose-response association between MVLTPA and risk of antihypertensive drug initiation was also observed (per 25 metabolic equivalent of task-minutes/day: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.97-1.00; p-value = 0.022). Conclusions: In older adults at high cardiovascular risk, MVLTPA was not associated with clinically meaningful differences in SBP or DBP trajectories or incident high blood pressure, but was associated with a lower risk of antihypertensive drug initiation. These findings support promoting habitual physical activity as part of cardiovascular risk management in older adults.

papers.title: Sputum quality and diagnostic outcomes of GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay among adults with presumed tuberculosis in two district hospitals in Ghana: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Ghana, where GeneXpert MTB/RIF serves as a first-line diagnostic tool. However, uncertainties about this method persist regarding specimen quality and the clinical significance of indeterminate rifampicin susceptibility results. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of samples from 3,977 presumptive TB patients tested either at HopeXchange Medical Center (Kumasi) or Keta Municipal Hospital between January 2020 and December 2024. Demographic data, sputum macroscopic appearance, and GeneXpert results were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Fishers exact test. Results: Overall Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTb) test positivity was 11.6% (461/3977). Males accounted for 63.3% of positive results, with the highest percentage among those ages 30-40 years. Mucopurulent specimens yielded the highest positivity rate (25.4%), compared to 4.0% of salivary specimens. Blood-stained sputum specimens (n=44) showed a 15.9% positivity rate. Although confirmed rifampicin resistance was low (1.7%), 9.3% of all MTb positive samples yielded an indeterminate result. The rate of indeterminate results from samples collected at Kwadaso Municipal increased from 7.3% in 2021 to 28.6% in 2024. Conclusion: These findings validate Ghana National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) guidelines emphasizing the reliability of mucopurulent specimen collection, but challenges the routine rejection of blood-stained sputum. The rising trend of indeterminate rifampicin results requires further investigation of circulating rpoB mutation profiles and quality assurance measures. Patients with indeterminate results should be further assessed using drug susceptibility testing to rule out rifampicin resistance. The findings provide actionable evidence to refine diagnostic algorithms and improve TB care in Ghana.

papers.title: Surge and decline of typhoid fever before and after a typhoid conjugate vaccine trial: a decade of blood culture surveillance in Asante Akim North, Agogo, Ghana
papers.abstract: Long surveillance series that follow typhoid fever through a surge and its aftermath are rare in Africa. Here, we describe ten years of blood culture surveillance in Agogo, Ghana; the period included a surge in 2017 and a cluster randomised trial of a typhoid conjugate vaccine in 2021-2022. We analysed 20,035 blood cultures from febrile patients enrolled between May 2016 and December 2025 at Asante Akim North, Agogo. Periods were identified by change point detection, and changes in positivity were estimated using segmented binomial regression. With the trial's household census as the denominator, we estimated detected incidence (culture confirmed cases detected per 100,000 person-years) among residents of the 15 trial communities. In total, 82 cultures (0.41%) grew Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi. Positivity rose from 2.77% (95% confidence interval 1.48-4.69) to 8.41% (6.05-11.31) during a surge between February and December 2017 and fell to 0.16% (0.11-0.22) from 2018. Thirty of 39 surge cases were children aged 5-14 years. Among residents, the detected incidence was 65.3 (45.3-91.3) per 100,000 person-years during the surge and 5.4 (2.5-10.2) in the post-surge years before vaccination. It was 5.9 (3.5-9.4) per 100,000 person-years after a campaign that vaccinated 87% of eligible children, while testing per head rose more than eight-fold. After adjustment for care seeking and blood culture sensitivity, incidence in 2016-2019 was 141 (104-189) per 100,000 person-years. Typhoid in Agogo fell sharply after 2017, three years before vaccination. Most of the later fall in test positivity reflects more testing rather than fewer cases. Thus, we recommend continued surveillance with population denominators.

papers.title: Kindergarten MMR Coverage, Vaccination Exemptions, and State-Level Measles Incidence in the United States, 2024 - 2026
papers.abstract: Objectives. To examine associations of kindergarten measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) coverage and vaccination exemptions with state-level measles incidence in the United States, 2024-2026. Methods. In this ecological study of 50 states and Washington, DC (up to 153 jurisdiction-years), we linked CDC surveillance, SchoolVaxView, and Census data. Negative-binomial models estimated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) per percentage-point increase for completed years 2024-2025 (generalized estimating equations) and through MMWR week 39, 2024-2026 (maximum likelihood, adjusted for density and poverty). Results. Cases rose from 269 (2024) to 2,263 (2025); 3,642 were reported provisionally through October 2, 2026. Completed-year IRRs were 0.875 (95% CI=0.806, 0.950) for MMR coverage, 1.202 (1.075, 1.344) for any exemption, and 1.207 (1.059, 1.376) for nonmedical exemption. Adjusted week-39 IRRs were 0.945 (0.837, 1.068), 1.147 (1.004, 1.310), and 1.131 (0.972, 1.316). Under cluster-robust maximum likelihood, completed-year intervals for MMR coverage and nonmedical exemption included 1. Conclusions. Higher exemption prevalence was associated with greater measles incidence; other estimates were imprecise. Public Health Implications. Monitoring exemptions alongside MMR coverage may help identify jurisdictions needing closer vaccination-gap assessment. Ecological findings do not establish causality.

papers.title: Observed Versus Modeled Data in GLOBOCAN 2024: Variation Across Cancer Sites and Implications for the Mortality-to-Incidence Ratio
papers.abstract: Purpose: The mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR) from GLOBOCAN is often used to compare cancer outcomes across countries. But in many countries, its two components come from different sources with some estimation methods deriving one from the other. We counted the countries in which both components of MIR are observed, and tested whether correlations between MIR and the Human Development Index (HDI) hold in them. Methods: Using GLOBOCAN 2024 data, we classed a country as having independent MIR when incidence came from cancer registries, mortality was observed, and neither was derived from the other. For each of 37 cancer sites, we calculated the fraction of global new cases occurring in these countries. We compared MIR-HDI Spearman correlations ({rho}) in these countries with the full sample, testing for attenuation beyond range restriction against an HDI-matched null distribution. Results: Only 41 of 186 countries (22%), all with high or very high HDI, had independent MIR. Of the 144 countries with derived MIR, 131 relied on external models. The independent-MIR fraction ranged from 0.12 (Kaposi sarcoma) to 0.77 (thyroid). For 33 of 37 sites, the correlation in independent-MIR countries was within what the narrower HDI range alone would produce. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, thyroid was the only site whose correlation weakened more than the narrower HDI range would explain ({rho} -0.82 to -0.004, adjusted p = 0.011). Conclusion: No low- or medium-HDI country has independent MIR, and in 131 countries at least one MIR component comes from an external model. Comparing MIR across these countries mostly compares model inputs. In independent-MIR countries, most MIR-HDI associations are consistent with range restriction but for thyroid, the association disappears.

papers.title: Influenza activity in the United States during the 2025-26 influenza season
papers.abstract: Background Comprehensive influenza surveillance is conducted year-round in the United States to monitor changes in influenza activity. This report summarizes the 2025-26 U.S. influenza season. Methods Data from September 28, 2025 through October 3, 2026 were collected from national surveillance systems monitoring influenza through laboratory testing, outpatient and emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and mortality. Data modeled disease burden and assessed severity using established criteria. A subset of influenza positive specimens were genetically and antigenically characterized and assessed for antiviral susceptibility. Results Influenza activity peaked during the week ending December 27, 2025, five weeks earlier than the 2024-25 season. There were two waves of influenza activity with influenza A(H3N2) subclade K viruses predominating the season overall and during the first wave followed by a smaller B/Victoria wave. The majority of circulating A(H3N2) and B/Victoria viruses were antigenically drifted from 2025-26 influenza vaccine reference strains. Season severity was classified as moderate overall, with children (0-17 years old) experiencing a high severity season and adults experiencing a moderate severity season. Children experienced the highest percent of influenza-associated outpatient and emergency department visits compared to other age groups. This season's cumulative influenza-associated hospitalization rate in children is the highest hospitalization rate in the past 16 years. Additionally, there were 198 influenza-associated pediatric deaths reported to CDC as of October 29, 2026. Conclusions Although antigenically drifted A(H3N2) viruses predominated, the 2025-26 U.S. influenza season occurred within historic norms for timing and severity. Year-round surveillance remains critical for detecting changes in influenza viruses and monitoring influenza-associated morbidity and mortality.

papers.title: Colorectal cancer incidence and mortality trends by age at onset in South Africa from 2002 to 2023
papers.abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer is the third most common cancer in men and women, and the fifth most common cancer overall, in South Africa. A previous report by the South African National Cancer Registry (SANCR) established that colorectal cancer incidence is rising in all South African population groups but rising fastest in Black South Africans. However, whether incidence increases by age at onset, as observed in many upper-income countries worldwide, remains unknown. In the present study, we assessed changes in colorectal cancer incidence (2002-2023) and mortality (2002-2019) in South Africa by sex, population group and age at onset. Methods: We calculated incidence from SANCR case counts and mortality from Stats SA death records, using Stats SA mid-year population estimates, standardised to the Segi world standard population. We defined age at onset as early (less than 50 years) or late (50 years or older). We described trends using joinpoint regression and annual percentage changes (APCs) over 2002-2023 and 2011-2023, the period after private-laboratory reporting became mandatory. Results: A total of 70,467 histologically confirmed primary colorectal cancers were registered with the SANCR over 2002-2023; 53.7% were in men. The overall age-standardised incidence rate (ASIR) was 6.61 per 100,000 (95% CI 6.32-6.89) in 2002 and 8.23 (7.99-8.46) in 2023. Overall incidence fell from 2002 to 2007 (not significant), rose from 2007 to 2015 and showed no significant change from 2015 to 2023. The first two segments coincide with the withdrawal of some private laboratories from reporting in 2005-2007 and with mandatory reporting from 2011. From 2011 to 2023, incidence fell in White South Africans (APC -1.0%, 95% CI -1.9 to -0.04), rose in Black African South Africans (+3.1%, 2.0 to 4.2) and did not change significantly in Coloured (-1.0%, -2.3 to 0.3) or Indian/Asian (+0.3%, -2.2 to 2.7) South Africans. Early-onset incidence rose by 1.6% per year (95% CI 1.1 to 2.1) over 2002-2023, similar to late-onset incidence (1.8%, 1.0 to 2.5). After 2011, neither changed significantly (early-onset +0.3%, -0.3 to 0.9; late-onset 0.0%, -1.0 to 1.0). Over 2002-2023, the early-onset APC was highest in White South Africans (+3.9%, 2.9 to 4.9), followed by Black African (+1.7%, 1.1 to 2.4), Coloured (+1.6%, 1.0 to 2.3) and Indian/Asian (+1.5%, 0.4 to 2.7) South Africans. The late-onset APC was +4.1% (3.4 to 4.9) in Black African, +1.3% (0.1 to 2.5) in White, +1.3% (0.1 to 2.5) in Indian/Asian and +0.7% (-0.3 to 1.6) in Coloured South Africans. After 2011, early-onset incidence rose in White (+1.2%, 0.3 to 2.2), Coloured (+1.7%, 0.4 to 3.1) and Black African (+1.1%, 0.4 to 1.8) South Africans. Late-onset incidence fell in White South Africans (-1.5%, -2.6 to -0.4) and rose in Black African South Africans (+3.7%, 2.4 to 5.0). Early-onset mortality rose by 1.2% per year (0.5 to 2.0) over 2002-2019, and late-onset mortality by 0.9% (0.3 to 1.4). Conclusion: Early-onset colorectal cancer incidence in South Africa rose over 2002-2023, and much of the rise coincided with mandatory private-laboratory reporting from 2011. Since 2011, early-onset incidence has risen modestly in White, Coloured and Black African South Africans, while late-onset incidence has fallen in White South Africans. In Black African South Africans, late-onset incidence and mortality continue to rise faster than early-onset.

papers.title: The plateau in liver disease mortality in Germany: contrasting trends by age, region and ICD-10 code, 2000-2024
papers.abstract: Background: Cirrhosis is often diagnosed only at decompensation, making identification of high-risk groups important for prevention and early detection. Chronic liver disease mortality has fallen in southern Europe and France since 2010, but not in Germany. Whether the German plateau reflects birth-cohort alcohol exposure, metabolic liver disease or certification practice is unknown. Methods: Deaths by ICD-10 code, sex and age group were extracted from the WHO Mortality Database for 16 European countries (2000-2022), with Eurostat rates (2011-2023), German state-level mortality (1998-2024) and hospital diagnoses (2000-2023). Registry and Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2023 estimates were summarised for ages 45-64, 65-74 and 75 years and over, with registry rates standardised to the European Standard Population 2013. Findings: Germany's age-standardised chronic liver disease mortality was 16.6 per 100 000 in 2011 and 16.0 in 2023, against declines of 21-37% in France, Italy and Spain. Between 2010 and 2022, alcoholic liver disease mortality at ages 45-64 fell by 17% in men and 25% in women, whereas fibrosis and cirrhosis (K74) mortality at ages 65-74 rose by 27% and 28%, with larger K70-K77 mortality increases in eastern than western Germany. Hospitalisation rates showed similar age-specific patterns, while in-hospital case fatality declined. Fewer than 0.5% of liver deaths were certified as fatty liver. GBD 2023 showed a similar age-specific increase but attributed rising mortality to all five modelled aetiologies. Interpretation: The German plateau reflects continued decline below age 65 and rising mortality at ages 65-74, compatible with cohorts born 1945-59 reaching this age band, particularly in eastern Germany. Consumption records and surveys indicate differing regional patterns of alcohol exposure. Much of the cirrhosis in these cohorts is certified without aetiology, and GBD's aetiological estimates cannot be verified in registration data. Funding: None.

papers.title: Delivered but Discharged Without Assessment: A National Multilevel Analysis of Missed Maternal Postpartum Assessment Before Discharge After Facility Birth in Ethiopia, 2024/2025 EDHS
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Missed maternal postnatal assessment before discharge after facility birth is an undermeasured indicator of intrafacility quality of care that previous Ethiopian studies did not isolate in nationally representative analyses. This gap matters because women may reach facilities for childbirth yet leave without a basic maternal clinical assessment during the highest-risk postpartum period, making missed assessment a marker of effective coverage failure rather than conventional postnatal care utilization alone. Methods: We analyzed nationally representative 2024-2025 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey data for 3,645 women aged 15-49 years whose most recent live birth occurred in a health facility. All analyses incorporated sampling weights and survey design features. Factors associated with missed maternal postnatal assessment before discharge were examined using multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression accounting for clustering within enumeration areas, with adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. Results: Overall, 40.1% (95% CI: 37.0-43.3) of women who delivered in Ethiopian health facilities did not receive a maternal postnatal assessment before discharge. Missed assessment was less likely after caesarean birth than vaginal delivery (AOR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53) and among women with at least one pregnancy complication (AOR 0.46, 95% CI 0.34-0.63). Antenatal care showed a dose-response association, with lower odds among women with 4-7 visits (AOR 0.49, 95% CI 0.27-0.89) and [≥]8 visits (AOR 0.43, 95% CI 0.23-0.81) than among women with no antenatal care. Geographic inequities persisted after adjustment, including higher odds in Somali (AOR 2.07, 95% CI 1.02-4.18). Conclusions: A substantial proportion of facility births in Ethiopia end without a maternal assessment before discharge, indicating that institutional delivery coverage can overestimate effective postpartum care when discharge processes are weak. Improving maternal outcomes will require universal pre-discharge assessment standards, stronger discharge documentation, and targeted quality-improvement efforts in underserved regions. For international maternal health policy, facility birth should not be counted as effective coverage unless every woman is assessed before she goes home.

papers.title: Cross-informant validation of the Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview in adolescents: Agreement between child and parent reports
papers.abstract: Background: Reliable assessment of avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) in young people may require information from both children and caregivers, yet cross-informant agreement has not been examined for the Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview (PARDI). This study evaluated agreement between child and parent PARDI interviews for ARFID diagnosis, individual DSM-5 Criterion A, ARFID dimensions, and overall severity. Methods: Twenty children aged 11-14 years screening positive for ARFID and one parent per child were recruited from the ARFID InitiativE Sweden (ARIES) cohort. Children and parents completed separate PARDI interviews with trained interviewers. Parent-child agreement was assessed using percentage agreement and Cohens kappa ({kappa}) for categorical ratings of ARFID diagnosis and Criterion A consequences. For continuous ratings of ARFID dimensions and overall severity, agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and paired t-tests comparing mean parent and child scores. Results: Parents gave higher mean scores than children across all continuous domains, although the difference was statistically significant only for overall severity (raw mean difference=0.42, p=.003). Parent-child agreement was poor for sensory sensitivity (ICC=0.42), moderate for lack of interest (ICC=0.63) and overall severity (ICC=0.71), and excellent for concern about aversive consequences (ICC=0.95). ARFID was identified in 17/20 parent interviews and 14/20 child interviews; diagnostic agreement was 75% ({kappa}=0.31, p=.133). Agreement was perfect (100%) for Criterion A1, high for A2 and A3 (both 95%), and lowest for psychosocial impairment (A4; 65% agreement, {kappa}=0.19). Item-level findings indicated a general tendency toward higher parental ratings, although children provided higher ratings on selected items involving food restriction, sensory experiences, hunger cues, and abdominal pain. Conclusions: Child and parent PARDI interviews provided overlapping but non-interchangeable information. Agreement varied across different aspects of ARFID, with greater discrepancies for psychosocial impairment and sensory sensitivity. These differences may partly reflect what children and parents are able to observe or experience directly. Multi-informant assessment may therefore offer a more complete account of pediatric ARFID than either response alone.

papers.title: Widening racial and ethnic disparities in Helicobacter pylori infection in the United States: a Bayesian meta-analytic catalytic model of age-specific forces of infection
papers.abstract: Background Helicobacter pylori is the main cause of non-cardia gastric cancer. In the U.S. H. pylori seroprevalence has declined. However, whether all subgroups have benefited equally from this change is unclear. Further, prevalence alone cannot indicate when infection risk is most acute and thus when to target prevention efforts like screening. Methods We synthesized age-stratified H. pylori seroprevalence data from 36 U.S. studies (N=56,845; 1965-2014), identified via literature search through September 2022. We fitted Bayesian hierarchical catalytic epidemic models to estimate, by race/ethnicity (for each of five race/ethnicity groups) and birth cohort (pre-1960 vs. 1960+, or continuous), the maximum proportion infected, age-specific force of infection (FOI), and the age at half-maximum seroprevalence. Findings Disparities in maximum prevalence worsened in the 1960+ birth cohort, with the absolute Hispanic-Non-Hispanic White (NHW) gap widening from 33.2 to 51.4 percentage points. FOIs peaked at the youngest ages for the Non-Hispanic American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) and Non-Hispanic Black (NHB) populations. Age patterns varied independently of burden; Hispanic and AI/AN populations reached similar peak prevalence (83.0% vs 76.1%) for the 1960+ birth cohort, yet the age at half-maximum seroprevalence was 19.3 years (95%CrI: 14.9, 23.5) vs 3.20 years (95%CrI: 1.99, 4.63). Continuous birth-cohort analyses supported these findings. Interpretation National declines in H. pylori mask widening racial and ethnic disparities. In AI/AN and NHB populations, seroprevalence rises steeply in early childhood, well before adulthood-targeted screen-and-treat programs would intervene. Moreover, similar peak prevalence can mask different age patterns of infection, and should be accounted for when guiding prevention strategies. Funding National Cancer Institute U01CA265729 and U01CA319219

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 antibody landscape following multiple vaccinations and infections during Omicron period
papers.abstract: Background: Repeated COVID-19 vaccination effects on the immunogenicity, breadth, and durability of antibody responses across antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants remain incompletely understood. Method: Participants receiving >= five COVID-19 vaccine doses 2020-2025 were selected from a prospective cohort in Michigan. Serum IgG, IgM, and ACE2 percent inhibition were measured using multiplex assays. Baseline-adjusted immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, and formulation-specific antibody durability were evaluated using regression models. Result: Twenty-one participants were included (median: seven vaccine doses). For every two-fold increase in pre-vaccination IgG concentration, post-vaccination fold-rise was 34% (95% CI: 16%-48%), 43% (95% CI: 15%-62%), and 55% (95% CI: 21%-75%) lower following monovalent, bivalent, and 2023-24 vaccination, while baseline-adjusted immunogenicity showed no significant trends across successive vaccines. Antibody landscapes demonstrated broad cross-reactivity against ancestral and Omicron variants, with similar strain-specific IgG changes across ancestral, vaccine-matched, and antigenically distant strains, but greater heterogeneity in ACE2 inhibition. Formulation-specific waning models showed significant IgG declines following monovalent and bivalent vaccination (beta = -1.03, 95% CI: -1.51 to -0.55; P<0.001 and -1.00 , 95% CI: -1.71 to -0.30; P=0.007, respectively) and ACE2 inhibition declines following monovalent vaccination, while other formulations showed less consistent changes. Despite waning, antibody levels generally remained relatively high across variants up to 300 days post-vaccination, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Conclusion: Repeated COVID-19 vaccination maintained baseline-adjusted immunogenicity and broad cross-reactive antibody responses, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Higher baseline immunity was associated with smaller post-vaccination increases, suggesting repeated boosting continues to reinforce humoral immunity despite increasingly complex immune histories.

papers.title: Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis Rates Among High-Risk Populations in Brazil: An Analysis from 2001 to 2021
authors: C. Dailton Guedes de Oliveira Moraes
papers.abstract: Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) represents a global public health threat, with a rising prevalence, particularly among vulnerable populations. This cross-sectional study analyzed MDR-TB notifications in Brazil from 2001 to 2021, using data from DATASUS, and stratified by periods and risk groups (HIV-positive individuals, smokers, drug users, healthcare workers, incarcerated individuals, and people experiencing homelessness). Descriptive analyses and parametric statistical tests (ANOVA and Tukey, p<0.05) were applied. A significant increase in cases was observed across all groups, especially between 2017 and 2021, with growth ranging from 294% to 574% depending on the population. Factors such as treatment abandonment, coinfection, social vulnerability, and occupational exposure were key determinants for MDR-TB dissemination. The findings indicate that current public health policies are insufficient, highlighting the urgent need for targeted prevention strategies, therapeutic follow-up, and control measures for high-risk populations.

papers.title: Multi-omics models for hypertension prediction using blood pressure PRS and omics scores
papers.abstract: BackgroundHypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the relative contributions of proteomic (ProtS), metabolomic (MetS), and polygenic risk scores (PRS) to incident hypertension risk remain incompletely characterized. MethodsWe developed ProtS and MetS for systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and hypertension using Elastic Net regression in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA). We incorporated these scores with previously developed BP PRSs into 5 incremental XGBoost models, with external validation in the Jackson Heart Study (JHS). We further applied transfer learning to adapt the MESA-derived models to JHS. Elastic Net selected proteins were prioritized using Mendelian randomization, colocalization, and functional analyses. ResultsIn MESA, model discrimination improved with the addition of omics scores, with the combined model achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.72 compared with 0.63 for the clinical baseline model. In JHS, ProtS showed the highest AUC of 0.68 and the smallest cross-cohort performance decline, compared to MetS and PRS. Incorporating measured SBP and DBP substantially improved discrimination, with the PRS+BP model achieving an AUC of 0.80 in MESA and the baseline+BP model achieving an AUC of 0.74 in JHS. Among JHS participants with normal baseline BP, ProtS provided the strongest discrimination among models without measured BP (AUC = 0.62), while PRS+BP model achieved an AUC of 0.69. Leaf-weight refreshing consistently improved calibration in JHS while preserving discrimination. Mendelian randomization identified 77 proteins associated with BP traits or hypertension, involved in vascular, inflammatory, renal, and natriuretic pathways. ConclusionsProtS demonstrated superior predictive performance and cross-cohort transferability among the omics modalities evaluated, while measured BP remained the strongest predictors of incident hypertension. Proteomic and genetic information may provide complementary biological signals for identifying individuals at elevated hypertension risk, particularly before clinically elevated BP is detectable.

papers.title: Beyond National Averages: Social Contact Patterns in the Upper Midwest
papers.abstract: BackgroundSocial contact surveys measure how individuals interact with each other, which directly influences disease transmission dynamics. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered how people live and work, highlighting the need for up-to-date and sub-national estimates of social contact patterns to inform disease modeling and public health planning. MethodsThe Midwest Analytics & Disease Modeling Center (MADMC) conducted an opt-in social contact survey of upper Midwest residents, with about 60% of participants drawn from Minnesota. Participants reported all interpersonal contacts during the previous day, including the age of their contacts allowing for the analysis of mixing patterns. Detailed demographic information about the participants was also collected, allowing for additional subgroup analyses of contact patterns. ResultsParticipants in our sample had an average of 6.8 contacts per day (IQR: 2.0 - 8.0), which is within the range of recent post-pandemic US national and European estimates. Contacts varied across demographic groups, with those attending work or school in-person reporting the highest number of contacts. Mixing across most age group pairs was a little lower than in comparable national survey except for younger age groups, who had substantially higher rates of contact with same-age peers. Differences in the contact matrices alone were associated with a 6.7% difference in estimated basic reproduction number(R0). Near the epidemic threshold, even this modest difference could meaningfully affect transmission dynamics. These effects may be amplified or attenuated by pathogen-specific age patterns of susceptibility and infectiousness, leading to larger or smaller differences in R0 estimates derived from national versus regional mixing patterns. ConclusionsThese findings provide empirical evidence on post-pandemic social contact patterns in the United States and highlight the potential implications of regional variation in social mixing for infectious disease transmission. The mean 6.8 daily contacts is consistent with evidence of persistent changes in daily routines following the pandemic. Incorporating contemporary, region-specific contact patterns into transmission models may improve their ability to capture geographic variation in transmission risk and inform epidemic forecasting.

papers.title: Wastewater sequence data reveal national and cross-border virus transmission dynamics
papers.abstract: Spatial epidemic models estimate disease transmission counts between populations using human mobility data, but location-to-location transmission is rarely observed directly. To address this gap, we develop mutation-counting methods to infer transmission structure from viral genetic variation measured in wastewater. In epidemic simulations with known transmission networks, our primary estimator robustly recovers spatial structure under realistic mutation-detection limits. Applied to spatiotemporal SARS-CoV-2 wastewater data from Austria, the method reveals strong seasonal reorganization, with inferred transmission becoming more geographically localized in winter and more dispersed in summer. We further identify locations with systematically higher or lower connectivity than expected from commuting, with temporal changes coinciding with regional restrictions, reopening and tourism. We then test whether such inference remains possible across national borders, recovering coherent spatial structure and temporal variation in connectivity between Austria, Switzerland and Liechtenstein. These results establish wastewater sequence data as a promising complement to mobility data for monitoring spatial transmission and detecting changes in epidemic spread associated with seasonality and interventions.

papers.title: Emergent Heterogeneity in Compartmental Disease Models
papers.abstract: Heterogeneity in infectious disease spread reshapes the risk and severity of outbreaks. This heterogeneity can arise from intrinsic individual-level differences in susceptibility, contact patterns, and infectious durations. Heterogeneity can also emerge from disease dynamics in a canonically homogeneous population, due to the fact that individuals randomly become infected at different times, recover after different intervals, and have access to different numbers of susceptible individuals. Here, we explore the mechanisms generating emergent heterogeneity by analyzing secondary case distributions within the SIR model. We show numerically and prove analytically that the variation in secondary cases, calculated over the course of the epidemic, does not change with R0. This is in contrast to the increasing variation in secondary cases in the linearized SIR model, often used to study heterogeneity at the beginning of an outbreak. When we consider "forward cohorts" of individuals infected at the same time, between-cohort variation increases as R0 increases, while within-cohort variation decreases. We show that these effects balance exactly, leading to the invariance of the variation in secondary cases with respect to R0. These results demonstrate the importance of considering emergent, as well as intrinsic, variation between individuals and of considering heterogeneity of transmission spread over the whole epidemic cycle, including substantive dynamical effects that appear even in the initial outbreak phase.

papers.title: Nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV hospitalizations in children 8-23 months at risk of severe RSV
papers.abstract: ImportanceRespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization in high-risk young children during their second RSV season. Nirsevimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody against RSV, is recommended for some children who are at increased risk for severe RSV and entering their second RSV season to prevent severe RSV disease. Because of limited eligibility criteria for second season nirsevimab, estimating its effectiveness is challenging. ObjectiveWe evaluated nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations among young children eligible to receive nirsevimab during their second RSV season. DesignThis retrospective case control study with a test-negative design was conducted during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 RSV seasons. SettingEnrollment was in 26 hospitals across 24 U.S. states. ParticipantsChildren eligible for nirsevimab during their second RSV season (as recommended in August 2023) were included. Nirsevimab-eligible children 8-23 months old hospitalized with respiratory symptoms were enrolled. Case-patients tested positive for RSV; control-patients tested negative for RSV. ExposuresReceipt of nirsevimab before or during the childs second RSV season and at least 7 days before symptom onset. Outcomes and measuresRSV-associated hospitalization. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, month and year of hospitalization, census region, and sex comparing the odds of second season nirsevimab receipt among case- and control-patients. ResultsOne hundred six case-patients and 125 control-patients were analyzed. Distributions of age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region were similar in case- and control-patients. Most case- and control-patients were eligible for nirsevimab because of chronic lung disease of prematurity (84.0% and 69.6%, respectively). Overall, 21 (19.8%) of case-patients and 53 (42.4%) of control-patients received nirsevimab. Adjusted nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 78.1% (95% CI, 55.2%-89.3%); the median interval from nirsevimab receipt to symptom onset was 66.5 days (IQR = 30-96 days). Effectiveness was estimated to be higher if nirsevimab was received 8-59 days before symptom onset (88.5%, 95% CI, 63.4%-96.4%). ConclusionsThis analysis provides real-world estimates of substantial nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations for high-risk U.S. children in their second RSV season These data support recommendations for nirsevimab as a preventive strategy in this population. Key PointsO_LIQuestion: What is the effectiveness of nirsevimab against RSV-associated hospitalizations among children 8-23 months old who are at risk for severe disease and in their second RSV season? C_LIO_LIFindings: In this case-control study of hospitalizations for acute respiratory illness among high-risk children in their second RSV season, receipt of nirsevimab was associated with an estimated 78% reduction in risk of RSV-associated hospitalizations. C_LIO_LIMeaning: Nirsevimab provided substantial protection against RSV-associated hospitalizations in children at high risk of severe RSV during their second RSV season. C_LI

papers.title: Population-level indirect effects of HPV vaccination in high-income settings: a Bayesian modelling study
papers.abstract: BackgroundHuman papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination provides direct protection to vaccinated individuals, but also indirectly protects unvaccinated individuals through reduced HPV transmission. Mechanistic transmission models that predict the magnitude of such effects have been crucial to informing vaccination strategies. However, nearly two decades of post-vaccination experience in high-income countries now allow us to empirically characterise how population-level indirect effects vary with vaccine coverage, time since vaccine introduction, and age. MethodsWe synthesised studies reporting HPV16/18 prevalence before and after vaccine introduction in high-income settings between 2007 and 2025. Indirect effects were estimated as the observed reduction in HPV16/18 prevalence after accounting for expected direct vaccine protection. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to examine associations with vaccine coverage, time since vaccine introduction, and age at effect assessment across routine, catch-up, and non-targeted vaccination groups. XGBoost was used as a complementary, non-parametric approach. FindingsData from 11 high-income settings were included. Indirect effects increased during the first five to eight years after vaccine introduction and then remained relatively stable. Indirect effects generally decreased with increasing vaccine coverage. Patterns with age differed across vaccination groups. In the routine group, indirect effects increased during adolescence and remained positive at older observed ages. In the catch-up group, indirect effects decreased with age and approached zero or became negative after approximately age 25 years. XGBoost identified similar non-linear patterns. InterpretationIndirect protection against HPV16/18 develops gradually after vaccine introduction and varies with vaccine coverage, age, and vaccination group. This empirical approach can complement transmission models by using real-world evidence to characterise population-level indirect protection. However, making predictions outside the populations and ranges represented in the data should be done cautiously. FundingThis study received no specific funding. Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSWe searched PubMed for studies published up to Oct 26, 2026. The search terms were ("HPV vaccin" [All Fields] OR "human papillomavirus vaccin" [All Fields]) AND ("herd immunity" [All Fields] OR "herd effect" [All Fields] OR "indirect effect" [All Fields] OR "indirect protection" [All Fields] OR "herd protection" [All Fields]). We included systematic reviews, meta-analyses, observational studies, and modelling studies that assessed the indirect effects of HPV vaccination on HPV infection or HPV-related outcomes. We excluded studies that focused exclusively on direct vaccine protection or economic evaluations that included herd immunity without separately estimating or reporting indirect effects. We identified 301 articles, of which 77 met the inclusion criteria: 52 observational studies, 22 modelling studies, and three systematic reviews or meta-analyses. From those studies, two systematic reviews by Drolet and colleagues (2015 and 2019) synthesised evidence from 14 high-income countries and provided evidence of herd protection following vaccine introduction. A meta-analysis of results from 16 transmission dynamic models by Brisson and colleagues (2016) projected substantial herd effects under different vaccination coverage levels. More recently, an observational study by Meglic and colleagues (2026) used nationwide registry data from Sweden and found age-varying herd effects, with lower incidence of high-grade cervical lesions among unvaccinated women in cohorts exposed to school-based vaccination. Despite growing real-world evidence from high-income countries over nearly two decades, few studies have examined how indirect protection varies with vaccination coverage, time since programme introduction, and age across settings. Added value of this studyTo our knowledge, this is the first study to synthesise real-world HPV16/18 prevalence data from 11 high-income settings to estimate the indirect effects of HPV vaccination over the period 2007-2025. Our findings show that indirect protection generally increases during the first several years after vaccine introduction before stabilising, with different patterns across age groups and vaccination programmes. Implications of all the available evidenceAs countries work towards cervical cancer elimination, understanding the indirect protection provided by HPV vaccination is important for assessing its broader population-level impact. This multi-country evidence complements transmission-dynamic models and provides an empirical basis for evaluating the long-term effects of HPV vaccination programmes.

papers.title: An integrative eco-entomovirological study of Culicoides species associated with Oropouche virus in Colombia
papers.abstract: BackgroundOropouche virus (OROV) causes recurrent outbreaks in South America, including Colombia. Although Culicoides paraensis is the principal recognized urban vector, the potential involvement of other Culicoides species remains incompletely understood. In Colombia, studies combining viral detection, host-feeding behavior, and ecological suitability are scarce. MethodologyWe investigated Culicoides communities in urban and peri-urban environments of Puerto Carreno, Vichada, during two seasonal transitions. Species identification combined morphology and COI DNA barcoding, and blood-meal sources were identified using vertebrate molecular markers. OROV RNA was assessed by RT- qPCR targeting the L and S genomic segments, and maximum likelihood prevalence estimates with 95% confidence intervals were calculated accounting for unequal pool sizes, including a conservative estimate based on concordant detection of both targets. Selected positive samples underwent multiplex amplicon sequencing fragments from all three OROV genomic segments (L, M, and S) using Oxford Nanopore Technology, followed by consensus reconstruction and phylogenetic analysis. Ecological suitability models were compared with reported OROV case distributions. Principal FindingsWe collected 1,639 specimens representing 11 taxa, eight supported by COI barcoding. C. insignis accounted for more than 70% of captures and was the only taxon collected in urban settings. OROV RNA was detected in C. insignis, C. pusillus, and C. ignacioi. In C. insignis, concordant detection of the L and S molecular targets yielded an estimated prevalence of 3.61 per 1,000 individuals (95% CI: 0.94-9.60). Nanopore sequencing recovered OROV-derived fragments spanning up to 656 nt across the L, M, and S genomic segments. Shorter fragments supported molecular identification, while phylogenetic analysis of a 656-nt M-segment region recovered from C. insignis and C. pusillus placed both sequences within a group containing viruses associated with the recent South American outbreak, although partial genomic coverage prevent formal lineage assignment. Blood-meal analyses identified feeding on humans, horses, and pigs in C. insignis; humans and horses in C. pusillus; and horses in C. ignacioi. Ecological models identified distinct environmental associations among species, and predicted suitability for overlapping portions of regions reporting OROV cases. Administrative-scale concordance was heterogeneous. ConclusionsThe integration of molecular, host-feeding, and ecological evidence highlights C. insignis, C. pusillus, and C. ignacioi as species of epidemiological interest in the context of OROV circulation in Colombia. These findings expand current knowledge of OROV-associated Culicoides diversity and provide a basis for targeted entomological surveillance and experimental studies to clarify their potential roles in virus transmission. Author SummaryOropouche virus (OROV) causes recurrent outbreaks in South America, including Colombia. Although Culicoides paraensis is the principal recognized urban vector, the possible involvement of other biting midge species remains poorly understood. We investigated Culicoides communities in urban and peri-urban environments of Puerto Carreno, eastern Colombia, combining species identification, blood-meal analysis, viral RNA detection, sequencing, and ecological modeling. OROV RNA was detected by RT-qPCR in C. insignis, C. pusillus, and C. ignacioi. Genetic sequencing confirmed the presence of OROV-derived sequences. Partial viral M segment sequences grouped with references associated with recent South American outbreaks, although they did not allow formal lineage assignment. C. insignis was the most abundant species, with repeated viral detections and evidence of feeding humans and domestic animals. Ecological models showed distinct environmental associations among species and variable overlap with regions reporting human cases. Together, these findings highlight the potential epidemiological relevance of multiple Culicoides species and provide a basis for targeted surveillance and experimental studies to clarify their roles in OROV transmission.

papers.title: Aging, Structural, and Neighborhood-Environmental Correlates of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Risk Factor Burden Across U.S. Census Tracts
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe American Heart Association defined Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome in 2023. Census-tract studies often examined one condition without spatial modeling. It is unclear where combined Stage 1-2 burden concentrates and how it relates to aging, environment, and socioeconomic conditions. MethodsWe built a CKM burden index for 70,336 tracts from five CDC PLACES crude prevalences (obesity, diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, chronic kidney disease) and compared it with NHANES 2017-2020. In 69,530 contiguous-U.S. tracts, we fit Bayesian spatial (BYM2) models with demographic, socioeconomic, and environmental predictors and aging x environment interactions, plus descriptive machine learning. The primary model excluded behavioral measures sharing the outcomes BRFSS source; a second added them. Credible intervals (CrIs) are conditional on PLACES estimates. ResultsAgreement with NHANES was modest. Burden clustered spatially (Morans I = 0.657) and highest in the South. Behavioral measures had the largest machine-learning importance (52.6%), partly from shared sourcing. Each percentage-point increase in adults [≥]65 years was associated with 0.112 units higher burden (95% CrI 0.111-0.113) outside low-income, low-access (LILA) tracts. LILA tracts had 0.10-0.14 units higher burden from the 25th aging percentile but not consistently in the youngest decile. Aging and socioeconomic associations held across sensitivity analyses. The primary models residual Southern excess approached zero after adding behavioral measures, which may reflect shared measurement, real differences in these behaviors, or both. ConclusionsCKM burden is spatially clustered and highest in the South. LILA tracts had modestly higher burden above the youngest tracts. These cross-sectional estimates support area-level surveillance and needs assessment. Clinical PerspectiveO_ST_ABSWhat Is New?C_ST_ABSO_LIAcross 69,530 US census tracts, a combined cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic burden index built from CDC PLACES was clustered in space and highest across the South. C_LIO_LIEach 1-percentage-point higher share of adults aged [≥]65 years was associated with 0.112 units higher burden (crude prevalence, not age-standardized). C_LI What Are the Clinical Implications?O_LITract-level burden maps can help health systems and public health agencies direct cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic screening and prevention to high-burden areas, including the South, as area-level needs assessment rather than individual risk prediction. C_LI

papers.title: Gut microbiome associations with incident cardiovascular disease in Nordic populations
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe gut microbiome is an emerging risk factor for cardiovascular disease. However, there is a lack of large-scale metagenomic studies with replication that identify gut microbial features associated with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD). MethodsWe tested for gut microbiome associations with CVD using metagenomes from stool samples in a discovery-replication framework across four large prospective Nordic cohorts with 635 incident CVD in 11,604 participants in the discovery cohort and 2,309 incident CVD in 20,965 participants combined across three replication cohorts. ResultsHigher Shannon diversity index and species richness were consistently associated with a lower risk of incident CVD. In addition, the relative abundance of nine species and eleven bacterial functional modules showed reproducible associations with incident CVD in the discovery cohort and in a meta-analysis of the three replication cohorts. We identified a female-specific gut microbiota-related pathway involving the prevalent oral-gut species Rothia mucilaginosa_A, enriched among denture users, thus serving as a proxy for longstanding poor oral health. Mendelian randomization analysis supported a causal effect of denture use on increased relative abundance of Rothia mucilaginosa_A. This pathway was linked to increased CVD risk through altered gut microbial manganese transport, elevated circulating imidazole propionate levels, and increased levels of systemic inflammation biomarkers. The second pathway involved both -diversity metrics and the remaining eight species, all of which were strongly associated with multiple markers of metabolic syndrome and with bacterial pathways related to purine metabolism, microbial stress responses, altered redox balance, ascorbic acid degradation, and branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis. ConclusionsThese findings demonstrate that gut microbiota diversity, specific taxa, and functional pathways provide new insights into the underlying biology of CVD. Furthermore, these findings suggest that the link between poor oral health and cardiovascular disease may, at least partly, operate through altered gut microbiota.

papers.title: The gut microbiome and incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular events: Prospective analyses in three Swedish cohorts
papers.abstract: BackgroundVariation in the gut microbiome composition has been associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in case-control designs. We aimed to investigate associations with incident ASCVD events applying a prospective design to reduce the impact of reverse causality. MethodsWe assessed associations between gut microbiome features measured by shotgun metagenomic sequencing and incident total ASCVD, ischemic heart disease (IHD) and ischemic stroke, including fatal and non-fatal events as defined by registry follow-up in 17,216 participants from three Swedish population-based cohorts (SCAPIS, SIMPLER, and MOS). Results from Cox proportional hazards regression models adjusted for demographic, and lifestyle factors, medication, and prevalent diabetes were combined across cohorts using a fixed-effect meta-analysis accounting for multiple testing. Associations were tested for replication in HUNT and FINRISK. ResultsDuring a median of 6-8 y follow-up, 769 incident ASCVD events occurred. Species diversity was inversely associated with ASCVD and IHD, with a hazard ratio for IHD of 0.86 per SD increase in species richness (95% CI: 0.79-0.95). Sixty-eight common species (i.e., present in [≥]30% individuals) were associated with incident IHD after adjusting for sex and birth country, but only eight remained in fully adjusted models, including Ruminococcus_B gnavus. Among others, inverse associations were observed for SFEL01 sp004557245 and Fimadaptatus sp900553645 from Christensenellales, an order in which butyrate production has been reported. Streptococcus mutans and Limosilactobacillus fermentum, oral-associated species previously associated with coronary atherosclerosis, were associated with a higher risk of incident IHD, which remained after adjustment for dental health. Replication analysis in the HUNT study supported the finding for S. mutans. No associations were observed with ischemic stroke. ConclusionsGut species diversity and specific species abundance were associated with incident IHD, providing evidence supporting a protective role of two Christensenellales species and an adverse role of oral species and R. gnavus in the development of IHD.

papers.title: Projected prevalence and number of persons with diagnosed type 2 diabetes by socioeconomic position in Germany between 2022 and 2060
papers.abstract: BackgroundCurrent projections of the prevalence and number of persons with type 2 diabetes by socioeconomic position (SEP) are lacking for Germany. This study aims to project age-specific type 2 diabetes prevalence in Germany by sex and SEP between 2022 and 2060. MethodsWe used a partial differential equation (PDE) based on the illness-death model to project age-specific type 2 diabetes prevalence by sex and SEP between 2022 and 2060. The PDE describes the relationship between prevalence, incidence, all-cause mortality and the mortality rate ratio (MRR) of individuals with vs. without type2 diabetes considering age, calendar year and SEP. SEP was measured by quintiles of the German Index of Socioeconomic Deprivation (GISD). Baseline prevalence, incidence, and MRR in 2022 were derived from statutory health insurance data ([~]85% of the German population). Projected prevalence was multiplied by population projections from the German Federal Statistical Office to estimate the number of persons with diabetes. ResultsType 2 diabetes prevalence increases with age, peaking between 80 and 90 years. Between 2022 and 2060, age-specific prevalence is projected to increase for both sexes across all SEP groups. SEP-related disparities persisted with largest differences between the highest (5th GISD quintile) and lowest (1st GISD quintile) SEP group. The number of persons with type 2 diabetes is projected to rise from 8.4 million in 2022 to between 11.2 and 19.2 million in 2060. ConclusionsBetween 2022 and 2060, age-specific type 2 diabetes prevalence is projected to increase with increasing socioeconomic inequalities.

papers.title: Investigating Differential Changes in Cardiovascular Mortality by Documented diabetes in the United States Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Comparative Time-Series Analysis
papers.abstract: BackgroundWhether diabetes modified pandemic-related changes in cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality remains uncertain. We examined differential changes in US CVD mortality among deaths with versus without diabetes documented on the death certificate. MethodsWe analyzed CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data from 2005 to 2024, identifying deaths with CVD as the underlying cause among adults aged [≥]25 years. Cohorts were CVD deaths with diabetes documented as a contributing cause (CVD+DM) and CVD deaths without documented diabetes. Because pre-2020 trajectories differed, the primary comparison of age-adjusted rates used a comparative interrupted time-series model allowing cohort-specific pre-2020 trends. Difference-in-differences estimates (2015-2019 vs 2020-2024) were descriptive. ResultsCVD+DM mortality declined from 43.1 per 100,000 in 2005 to 34.3 in 2019 and was 38.4 in 2024; mortality without documented diabetes declined from 398.7 to 296.6 and was 289.8. In the primary analysis, CVD+DM mortality showed a 13.1% greater relative level increase at 2020 (95% CI, 10.4%-15.9%), with no significant differential change in slope thereafter. Descriptively, the ratio of rate ratios was 1.16, and the absolute difference-in-differences was 5.0 per 100,000. ConclusionsAfter accounting for cohort-specific pre-2020 trends, CVD mortality with documented diabetes showed a greater relative increase at the 2020 transition. These findings describe differential mortality patterns rather than a causal effect of diabetes or the pandemic. WHAT IS NEW?O_LICardiovascular disease mortality with documented diabetes showed a 13% greater relative level increase at the 2020 transition than cardiovascular disease mortality without documented diabetes, after accounting for pre-2020 trends. C_LIO_LIThe difference was concentrated in the level change around 2020, with no significant differential change in slope thereafter. C_LIO_LIFindings were directionally consistent across analyses using alternative baseline periods, breakpoints, and restriction to type 2 diabetes. C_LI WHAT ARE THE CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS?O_LIThe findings suggest that people with coexisting cardiovascular disease and diabetes may warrant particular attention during periods of major health system disruption, including efforts to maintain continuity of cardiometabolic care. C_LIO_LIBecause the analysis is based on death-certificate documentation, the findings should be interpreted as a population-level mortality signal rather than evidence that diabetes caused the observed mortality difference. C_LI

papers.title: Sex specificity in DNA Methylation Profiles of Neonates Following Early Preterm Birth
papers.abstract: Preterm birth (PTB) affects 11% of pregnancies worldwide, yet the biological mechanisms underlying its etiology remain unclear. We conducted a sex-stratified epigenome-wide association study of newborn saliva DNA methylation in 273 mother-child pairs from the Peruvian Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology (PAGE) study. Robust linear regression models adjusted for maternal, cellular, and technical factors identified 318 and 542 ePTB-associated CpG sites and 784 and 1,401 differentially methylated regions in boys and girls, respectively, with limited overlap between sexes. Functional analyses revealed enrichment of signals in Open Sea regions and pathways related to neurodevelopment, neural function, fetal growth, cellular organization, transcription factors, and microRNAs. Several associations replicated findings from prior studies of PTB, gestational age, and post-menstrual age. These results identify sex-specific epigenetic signatures of ePTB in an Admixed-American population and highlight developmental and regulatory pathways associated with ePTB.

papers.title: A deterministic framework for linkage of infectious disease surveillance and national mortality records: development and validation using tuberculosis surveillance data
papers.abstract: BackgroundLinkage of infectious-disease surveillance data to mortality records is important for estimating long-term outcomes, but incomplete personal identifiers present methodological challenges. We developed and validated a deterministic linkage framework for linking the National Tuberculosis Surveillance System (NTBS) with Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality records. MethodsTB notifications in England from 2001-2024 were linked to ONS mortality records using 12 sequential matching rules based on combinations of NHS number, date of birth, name, postcode, sex and phonetic matching. Linkage outputs underwent person-level deduplication and clerical review. Precision and recall were estimated, and potential linkage bias assessed by variation in identifier completeness and linkage success. Confirmed false-positive links identified during validation were removed from the analytical dataset. ResultsAmong 151,965 TB notifications, 28,060 initial links were identified. Following deduplication, validation and refinement, 26,937 linked notifications were retained. Estimated precision increased from 97.7% to 99.2% (95% CI 96.8-100.0) following removal of false-positive links; estimated recall was 98.1% (95% CI 95.4-98.6%). More than 90% of links used NHS-number-based match keys. PDS enrichment increased NHS-number availability and enabled additional NHS-number-based links, although a small proportion linked to different ONS records following enrichment. NHS number availability and linkage success differed across demographic and social groups, demonstrating differential linkage. ConclusionsA hierarchical deterministic approach combined with targeted validation achieved high linkage accuracy while identifying and addressing differential linkage. This provides a transparent framework for future NTBS-ONS linkage and may be adaptable to other surveillance systems where comparable identifiers are available. Key messagesO_LIHierarchical deterministic linkage achieved high precision (>99%) and recall (>96%) when linking tuberculosis notifications to mortality records. C_LIO_LIValidation demonstrated that high linkage accuracy can be achieved using routinely collected identifiers within national surveillance data. C_LIO_LIThe validated linkage provides a robust framework for mortality ascertainment and long-term outcome monitoring within tuberculosis surveillance. C_LI

papers.title: Real-world effectiveness of nirsevimab over three RSV seasons in an integrated health care system: a target trial emulation study
papers.abstract: Most nirsevimab effectiveness estimates come from test-negative designs, which restrict populations to those seeking healthcare and testing. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness among infants six months post-receipt using a target trial emulation with an estimand aligned to phase 3 trials. We emulated a target trial among infants born from February 2, 2023 through May 30, 2026, using electronic medical records at Kaiser Permanente Georgia. Using a g-computation estimator with Cox models fit separately in nirsevimab recipients and non-recipients, we estimated the cumulative incidence of RSV hospitalization and medically-attended RSV at 30-day intervals through 180 days post-receipt. Among 4,826 infants, nirsevimab reduced the risk of RSV hospitalization by 95% (95% CI: 84% to 98%) and medically-attended RSV by 67% (95% CI: 45% to 80%) at 180 days post-receipt. The number needed to immunize to prevent one case was 147 (95% CI: 94 to 333) for RSV hospitalization and 39 (95% CI: 28 to 68) for medically-attended RSV. Nirsevimab was effective through 180 days post-receipt. This cohort-based emulation avoids conditioning on testing and the restricted generalizability of the test-negative and matching-based designs that dominate the literature. These findings support continued nirsevimab use to protect infants against RSV.
